opening_message:
Ticket 1: Maurice Perez (employee ID E036) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E036.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Maurice Perez (E036) is a full_time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full_time employee, up to write is allowed (admin would require role ownership). Grant requested level: write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E036 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training (never admin). Requested write exceeds maximum; grant maximum: read.
reason: The two team notes conflict on employment type: HR DB says E036 is full_time Engineer (would allow write for Source Code), while Security DB says E036 is a contractor with basic security training (contractors get read, write only with advanced training). Given the conflicting records, I apply the more restrictive policy interpretation: as a contractor with basic training, the maximum is read, and the requested write exceeds that maximum. Grant read.
